title: 10th Sitting of First session of 2026
presiding: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim, as named in the minutes (the roster lists the Deputy Speaker as Ahmed Saleem, Eydhafushi)
summary: After opening prayers and the attendance and agenda announcements, the Majlis held the preliminary debate on the government-sponsored bill to amend the Fisheries Act (Law 2019/14), introduced by the member for South Thinadhoo. The bill adds administrative penalties for unlicensed fishing, requires management plans for fish species and lets the ministry develop fishing ports. Sixteen more members spoke after the sponsor, with most backing the aim while ruling-party and opposition members traded criticism over past and present fisheries policy, fuel and fish prices, loans for fishers, foreign crew and the ministry's new powers. A 30-minute recess was taken from 10:31 to 11:01 and the debate carries on into the next part. Attendance figures in the printed text were too garbled to read reliably, so they are left blank. This part picks up the debate on a bill to amend the Fisheries Act: government-side members backed it and pointed to payments to fishermen, while an MDP member raised concerns about broad ministerial powers and higher fines. The chair paused that debate to take a committee report on a privilege complaint by North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim, who had asked to visit a special-needs care centre in K. Guraidhoo. That debate widened into an argument over whether ministries and state companies answer MPs' questions. After a one-hour recess the amended report passed 57-0 and the next sitting was set for 22 April 2026 at 9:00 am. Parts of the text are garbled, so some details are uncertain.

items.title: Imtiyaz and Sulook Committee report on the privilege complaint filed by North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim (Rule 208)
Announcement of next sitting and close of sitting
items.outcome: next sitting set for 22 April 2026 at 9:00 am

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Traced the fisheries law from 1987, supported the bill, and asked that fishers take part directly when the bill goes to committee.
Opposed the report; said the care centre houses vulnerable people, visits need permission, and the complaint wasted the Majlis's time.
Said MPs' access rights cover places like prisons, not care centres, and that ministers do answer MDP members' calls.
Rejected the privilege complaint as politically motivated; disputed claims that government bodies are unaccountable.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Traced fisheries from the 1970 engine rollout, said it has slipped in the economy, and welcomed the government's fuel limits and plan to settle fishers' arrears.
Alleged such complaints are repeatedly brought to take up Majlis time and to undermine the government and state institutions.
Said he would not support the report and backed the Baarashu member's view.
Alleged opposition members left the chamber when government members began to speak.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Backed the bill, arguing fisheries should be built up as local production and that foreign workers and imports have grown too large a share of the sector.
Said MPs should use their privileges within set procedures, and that the report calls for faster information sharing between institutions.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the amendment but said past and current governments should act on fisheries promises, including repairing the ice plant at Noonu Lhohi and helping youth into fishing.
Supported the amended report; said the committee agreed on changes requiring ministries to reply in writing and arrange access to information.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Backed the main amendments and welcomed offshore platforms and home-based fish factories, but asked for catch limits on sports fishing and questioned price and fuel promises.
Said MPs have a constitutional right to question ministers, and that companies like HDC lack a clear way to answer to the Majlis.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Backed the bill in general and said Maldivians should get maximum benefit from sea resources rather than only restricting use.
Questioned rules agreed through the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, such as drone bans, saying they reduce fishing efficiency.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Fully backed the Fisheries Act amendments; said past governments failed fishermen while this one is paying them what is owed.
As the committee's reporting member, presented the privilege report on the Galolhu North member's request to visit a Guraidhoo care centre.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said PNC members' praise of ministers does not match the President's call for resignations after the election results.
Said oversight of the government is a constitutional duty of MPs, not optional.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the Galolhu North member files many urgent motions and privilege cases, which he alleged serve political ends.
Said entry to a protected care centre needs permission like any institution, and the report was amended so the government could support it.

speakers.name: Mohamed Alsan Ahmed
positions: Introduced the bill on behalf of the government: administrative action against unlicensed fishing, mandatory management plans for species, and ministry powers to develop fishing ports.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the amendment, welcomed the government's work on fishing-industry recovery and urged more research on marine resources using modern technology.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the amendment and asked for off-season income, insurance, easier bank lending for fishers and more opportunities for young people entering fishing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said law changes must come with practical help for fishers, including relief on their large loans, and opportunities for youth such as big-game fishing.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the amendments and raised delays in fuel supply to fishers, an unpaid fuel bill owed by MIFCO, and fish-pricing problems at purchase points.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Strongly supported the bill, welcomed consultation with fishers, and said fishers need good markets, fair prices and planning for sustainable use of the sea.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Questioned why the bill was rushed and warned it shifts Majlis powers to the ministry and could allow marine resources to be sold off; hoped committee stage would fix it.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Proposed a fixed allowance for registered fishers in place of subsidies and urged curbing reclamation and resort leases that damage fishing grounds.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the bill adds fees, large fines and court action for fishers, and that the sponsor gave no reasons for article 25 and other changes.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said the bill appears drafted without consulting fishers and stakeholders, asked for an impact assessment, and warned the changes could harm the industry.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Rebutted opposition criticism, citing higher fish prices, payment to fishers within 48 hours and fuel supply, and said foreign labour in the big skipjack fleet needs addressing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said the amendments open fishing to more people but that subsidies reach only some areas; argued Male' Atoll fishermen should get them fairly.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the amendments hand most powers to the minister without defining them, raise fines sharply, and that laws stall when regulations are never made.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Supported the amendments; said he was surprised the opposition resisted a fishermen's bill and that money owed to fishermen is now being paid.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said his privilege complaint, filed June 2025, took about ten months to conclude, and that ministries often leave MPs' letters and questions unanswered.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: As a committee member, said the report found no neglect of the member's privilege; the Health Ministry could grant access only under the centre's rules.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to describing a member's motions as film or drama; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

decisions: The chair set four hours of total debate time on the bill, divided among parties and independent members.
The chair paused the Fisheries Act amendment debate to take agenda item 6; it was not resumed in this part.
The Majlis passed the Imtiyaz and Sulook Committee report on North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim's privilege complaint, 57 for and none against (29 needed).
Next sitting announced for 22 April 2026 at 9:00 am.

votes.what: Passing the Imtiyaz and Sulook Committee report on the privilege complaint filed by North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim (93 members in total, 58 present, 57 voted, 29 needed)
